title: Damascus steel: the sword made from Indian steel

facts.claim: Wootz was a crucible steel made in South India, exported for centuries
Blades forged from wootz in the Middle East became known as Damascus steel, famous for a wavy surface pattern
The knowledge of making true Damascus blades was lost by around the 18th-19th century
In 2006 researchers at TU Dresden reported carbon nanotubes in a 17th-century Damascus sabre
The word 'wootz' is linked to South Indian words for steel such as Kannada 'ukku'

opening.why: The subject is an object (the blade); the wavy steel pattern is the hook, not a place.

music_mood: forge-and-mystery: slow pulse, metallic hits on reveals

headline: NOBODY COULD
COPY THIS SWORD
cover.hook_voiceover_ml: ഈ വാൾ 200 വർഷം ലോകത്ത് ആർക്കും പകർത്താനായില്ല. എന്തുകൊണ്ടെന്നോ?
cover.visual: A curved sabre blade fills the frame diagonally; its surface shows a flowing, wavy watered-steel pattern that shimmers.
cover.build_cmd: Dark charcoal background with a faint warm glow top-right. Draw one curved sabre (blade from x0.15,y0.62 to x0.85,y0.30, a slight curve, 60px wide, golden crossguard near the lower end). Fill the blade with a wavy 'watered steel' pattern: 25 horizontal sine-wave bands (amplitude 6px, wavelength 90px) in alternating light grey #d8dce4 and dark grey #6a7080, clipped to the blade shape. Over the whole reel a soft highlight band sweeps along the blade every 2.0s. From t=0 to 25% the blade slides in from the left with ease-out; keep top 20% and bottom 25% of the frame uncluttered.

scenes.voiceover_ml: നൂറ്റാണ്ടുകൾക്ക് മുമ്പ് ദക്ഷിണേന്ത്യയിൽ ഉണ്ടാക്കിയിരുന്ന ഒരു പ്രത്യേക ഉരുക്ക്. അതിന്റെ പേര് വൂട്സ്. കന്നഡയിലെ 'ഉക്കു' എന്ന വാക്കിൽ നിന്നാണ് ആ പേര്.
scenes.headline: WOOTZ: INDIA'S STEEL
scenes.visual: A clay crucible glowing in a furnace; ingots of steel cool on the ground; a simple south-India outline glows behind.
scenes.build_cmd: Background: deep brown-black. Centre: a clay crucible (rounded pot, x0.5 y0.48, 260px wide) sitting in orange flames (10 flame tongues, flicker with rand per frame but deterministic by t). Inside the crucible a molten disc glows from orange to white over the first 50%. From 55% a dark grey ingot (rounded rect 200x90) slides out to the right and cools: colour from #f2a53a to #8a8f98 by 90%. Behind everything, a faint outline of peninsular India (simple polygon, 0.35 opacity) at x0.5 y0.45, pulsing glow.

scenes.voiceover_ml: കപ്പലുകളിലും ഒട്ടകപ്പുറത്തും ഈ ഉരുക്ക് മിഡിൽ ഈസ്റ്റിലേക്ക് പോയി. അവിടെ ഡമാസ്കസിലെ കൊല്ലന്മാർ അതിൽ നിന്ന് വാളുകൾ തീർത്തു.
scenes.headline: SHIPPED TO DAMASCUS
scenes.visual: A trade route animates from south India across the Arabian Sea to the Middle East; small ship and camel icons travel along it.
scenes.build_cmd: Background: parchment-dark navy map feel (#0f1a2b) with faint grid. Draw two simple landmasses as soft polygons: India (right, x0.6-0.9, y0.35-0.65) and Arabia/Levant (left, x0.15-0.5, y0.3-0.55), fill #243649. A dashed route (accent colour, 5px, dash 18/12) draws progressively from (0.72,0.55) curving across the sea to (0.32,0.38) between 10% and 70% of the scene. A small ship (triangle sail + hull) rides the route from 10% to 45%; a small camel silhouette (simple rectangles) continues over land from 45% to 70%. At 70% a sword glyph (short line + crossguard) pops at the end point with a ring pulse.

scenes.voiceover_ml: ആ വാളുകൾക്ക് ഒരു പ്രത്യേകതയുണ്ടായിരുന്നു. വെള്ളം ഒഴുകുന്നത് പോലെ ഒരു അലയടയാളം. മൂർച്ചയും കരുത്തും കൊണ്ട് ലോകം മുഴുവൻ അതിനെ ഭയപ്പെട്ടു.
scenes.headline: THE WAVY PATTERN
scenes.visual: Extreme close-up of the blade surface; the wavy pattern flows like water; a drop of water ripples across it.
scenes.build_cmd: Fill the middle band (y0.25-0.7) with the blade close-up: 40 flowing bands made of sine waves whose phase drifts with t (speed 0.4), alternating #e6e9ef and #5c6472, with a subtle metallic gradient overlay. At 40% a water-drop ellipse falls from y0.2 to y0.47 (ease-in) and on landing three expanding ripple ellipses spread (stroke white, fading). Edge-light the top and bottom of the band with thin accent lines. Keep the band centred; blur-free, crisp shapes.

scenes.voiceover_ml: പിന്നെ സംഭവിച്ചത് വിചിത്രമാണ്. ഏകദേശം 1800-ഓടെ ആ ഉരുക്ക് ഉണ്ടാക്കുന്ന വിദ്യ തന്നെ നഷ്ടപ്പെട്ടു. ആർക്കും അതേ വാൾ പിന്നെ ഉണ്ടാക്കാനായില്ല.
scenes.headline: THE RECIPE WAS LOST
scenes.visual: A page of a recipe book burns to ash from the corner; an anvil with a half-made blade goes cold.
scenes.build_cmd: Background dark. Centre: a parchment page (rect 560x420 at x0.5 y0.42, #e8dcc0) with 7 faint text lines (grey rects). From 15% to 75% the page burns from the bottom-right corner: an irregular dark edge advances diagonally with a glowing orange rim (3px) and 20 ember particles drifting up (deterministic). Below the page, a small anvil silhouette (y0.68) with a blade on it; its glow fades from orange to cold grey over the scene. At 80% the whole page is gone; only ash flecks remain.

scenes.voiceover_ml: 2006-ൽ ജർമ്മനിയിലെ ഗവേഷകർ ഒരു പഴയ ഡമാസ്കസ് വാൾ മൈക്രോസ്കോപ്പിൽ നോക്കി. അതിനുള്ളിൽ കണ്ടത് കാർബൺ നാനോട്യൂബുകൾ! നമ്മുടെ പൂർവികർ അറിയാതെ ചെയ്ത നാനോ ടെക്നോളജി.
scenes.headline: NANOTUBES INSIDE
scenes.visual: A microscope zoom: the blade surface magnifies step by step until a lattice of tiny tubes appears, glowing.
scenes.build_cmd: Three zoom levels as nested frames: 0-30% the blade edge (grey band); 30-60% a circular 'lens' (radius 360px at x0.5 y0.46) showing grain texture (random dots); 60-100% inside the lens, 14 hexagonal-mesh tubes (cylinders drawn as repeated hexagon rows, accent colour, 0.8 opacity) fade in and gently rotate. Each zoom step uses a quick scale-in (0.8 to 1.0, ease-out, 0.4 s) and a thin crosshair. End with the tubes glowing (radial accent gradient) and a slow pulse.

instagram_caption:
The world's most legendary sword was made from Indian steel. ⚔️

Wootz, a crucible steel from South India, was shipped to the Middle East, where Damascus smiths forged blades with a famous wavy pattern. Then the recipe was lost, and in 2006 scientists found carbon nanotubes inside an old Damascus sabre. 🔬
